_note:
PROPOSED FRAGMENT for the renderer's kit — NOT a replacement for the renderer's own kit/roles.json, which holds hostRoles, hostPoses, roomRoles, chapterTypes, purposes and wardrobe and is what makes room/talk resolve to one of three desk angles by seed. This file is deliberately named roles.fragment.json so a copy operation cannot overwrite that one. Merge the entries below into the renderer's vocabulary by hand.

VOCABULARY: every chapter_types, shot_ids, formats and beats value in this file was read off templates/ and resolves against the real vocabulary recorded in _vocabulary below. The stale-vocabulary warning that stood here is answered — 44 of the 60 entries named invented chapter types or invented shot templates and have been mapped; the mapping table is in CHANGES.md §VOCABULARY. Nothing was deleted to make the count clean and no new chapter type was invented to make an entry fit.

_vocabulary.read_from: templates/chapters/*.json (one file per chapter type) and templates/shots/{short,earnings,macro,long}.json. This block is the list the entries below were checked against; it is a record, not a source — templates/ is the source.
_vocabulary.chapter_types_are_complete: sixteen, and there are no others. A plate that wants a seventeenth is a proposal for CHANGES.md, not a value in this file.
_vocabulary.shot_ids: PER CHAPTER, NOT GLOBAL. Each chapter file is a small shot list with structural ids: open, evidence, land, plus on-the-desk in filing-walk. shot_ids below names which structural position in a chapter's list the plate is for. There is no full-plate / push-in-on-plate / plate-with-host-medium / two-shot vocabulary anywhere in the codebase; the nine names this file used to carry were invented wholesale and are gone.
_vocabulary.how_host_framing_is_now_said: the constraint those invented names were really carrying — whether a plate survives sharing the frame with the host — is a property of the plate, so it is stated in the plate's own note as prose ('not for a shot that shares the frame with the host'). It was never a template name.

beats.long: NO BEATS OF ITS OWN. templates/shots/long.json holds none — the director picks chapter types and each expands to its own shot list. A long-form plate is placed by chapter_types + shot_ids; formats: ["long"] on an entry means only 'this plate is for long-form', and carries no beat.

_vocabulary.short_beats_are_not_chapter_types: the nine short-the-* values this file used to carry were SHORT beats wearing chapter-type clothing. They now sit under formats: ["short"] + beats: [...]. A portrait plate usually keeps a chapter_types value as well, for a long-form 9:16 cut.
_vocabulary.any: a plate that genuinely belongs everywhere says so with "any": true (and "any_shot": true for shot position) rather than with a "*" or an "any LONG chapter" string. A wildcard string does not resolve against sixteen names and the gate cannot check it. host/sitting-at-desk carries it; the host poses placed by rotation carry any_shot.
_vocabulary.moat: UNREFERENCED. Of the sixteen, moat is the one chapter type no plate in the kit reaches — see CHANGES.md §VOCABULARY. It is a gap in the LIBRARY, not in this file, and it is not fixed by adding moat to a plate that is not about a moat.
_vocabulary.field_shapes: LIST FIELDS HOLD NAMES, NOT SENTENCES. chapter_types, shot_ids, formats and beats are lists of vocabulary names — lowercase, hyphenated, no spaces — and anything iterating them expects that. An explanation belongs in note. Two entries (overlays/lower-third, both aspects) carried a sentence in beats; it was correct prose in the wrong field, and anything walking beats got a paragraph where a beat name belongs. Both are moved to note and their beats field is now ABSENT rather than empty, because the plate genuinely has no beat: it is persistent furniture composited over whatever the format is showing. An empty list would read as 'no beats found', which is a different claim.
_vocabulary.sectors: ROUND TWO AND THREE. sectors lists GICS sector names, lowercase and hyphenated: energy, materials, industrials, consumer-discretionary, consumer-staples, health-care, financials, information-technology, communication-services, utilities, real-estate. It names the kind of issuer a plate’s STRUCTURE presumes. Absent means any sector, which covers every plate before round two.
_vocabulary._rebuild21: Corrected at source, rebuild-21. 46 aspect-suffixed keys folded onto their asset ids (marks, overlays/row-band, host strips, rebuilt rooms, hook cards carry no aspect: one plate composites into both). 4 entries removed for assets the rebuild dropped (host/close-up-blink, host/empty-chair, room/over-the-shoulder-16x9 and -9x16). 24 entries carried shot_ids that are not structural positions in any chapter file (host, news-*, move-*, earnings-*, hook, closing): short and earnings ones now say formats + beats, host poses say any_shot. Every shot_ids value in this file is now one of open / evidence / land / on-the-desk.

_furniture.section: §1 — the persistent furniture. overlays/lower-third-{16x9,9x16}, plus the caption decision (not a plate; see CHANGES.md §1.2).
_furniture.lower_third: NOT a chapter plate and not in any chapter's shot list. It is furniture the renderer composites over whatever is on screen, so it belongs to the FORMAT rather than to a chapter — present for the whole of long and earnings, and at the director's discretion in short. It replaces render_long.py:1450 simple_text().
_furniture.captions: DECIDED: deliberately a different register — the kit's materials without its hand. force_style in CHANGES.md §1.2. Not a plate, so no chapter mapping.

overlays/lower-third-16x9.note: §1.1. Its own size, not a frame: the compositor places it, bottom-left at about one panel-height of margin, which is what it was designed against. Two slots — ticker (6 characters measured) and tagline (49) — replacing one PIL-formatted string. Persistent furniture, not a beat — which is why this entry carries no beats field at all: it is composited over whatever the format is showing, for as long as the director leaves it up. It reaches its formats directly.
overlays/lower-third-16x9.no_boil: one frame, and every mark is pinned. On screen longer than any other asset in the product; a re-wobble three times a second for forty minutes is a crawl, not craft.
overlays/lower-third-16x9.carries_own_ground: opaque panel, own rim, own cast. It composites over rooms, charts and filing screenshots — there is no wall to borrow legibility from. Same finding as §1's title card, applied where it is unarguable.
overlays/lower-third-16x9.purpose: a name-and-context strip composited over a room or plate.
overlays/lower-third-16x9.caution: Currently unreachable in both aspects — confirm the format uses a lower third before naming it.

overlays/lower-third-9x16.note: re-authored, not scaled: proportionally wider and a type step up, because it is read on a phone at arm's length. Ticker budget 8 characters against 6 in landscape. Persistent furniture, not a beat, so no beats field — and on a short it is the director's call whether the plate carries one at all.
overlays/lower-third-9x16.purpose: a name-and-context strip composited over a room or plate.
overlays/lower-third-9x16.caution: Currently unreachable in both aspects — confirm the format uses a lower third before naming it.

_confession.section: §2 — the confession. structure/confession-{statement,ledger}, both aspects each. Roughly one video in three carries one; the pipeline tracks them in a ledger and on screen it has been reaching for whatever generic plate the chapter had.
_confession.both_ship: unlike §1's title ground these are not mutually exclusive — a chapter can reach for either. RECOMMENDATION: ledger. Reasoning in CHANGES.md §2.
_confession.not_said_happened: structure/said-happened is a COMPANY's claim against the outcome and is built to read as an indictment. Pointing it at the host would make the plate an indictment of him, which is the opposite of what a confession is for.

_pipelineData.section: §3 — five plates the pipeline already has data for. Ten assets built: figures/short-interest, charts/insider-flow-{6,12}, charts/macro-series, structure/end-card, both aspects each. 3.5 (channel art) is NOT built — see CHANGES.md, it needs a decision rather than a plate.
_pipelineData.vocabulary: these entries use the REAL sixteen chapter types, the real per-chapter shot ids (open / evidence / land / on-the-desk) and the real format beats. The older entries in this file do not — see the stale-vocabulary warning in _note.

_timeOfDayShipped.section: §4.2 — time of day, shipped as ASSETS rather than as a mode. 24 new keys: room/<angle>-dusk-{16x9,9x16} for all twelve angles.
_timeOfDayShipped.how_to_use: the director picks an hour per EPISODE by picking keys — exactly as roomRoles already resolves `talk` to one of three desk angles by seed. Add the -dusk keys to a role's list to let an episode draw from them, or swap the role's list wholesale for a dusk episode. Do NOT mix hours inside one video: two hours on one wall in one video is two rooms.
_timeOfDayShipped.identical_geometry: verified, not asserted: every -dusk plate has byte-identical slot boxes, floorLineY and hostAnchor to its night twin. Only the wall tone differs. So a shot template that works on room/desk-front-16x9 works on room/desk-front-dusk-16x9 with no changes at all.
_timeOfDayShipped.unblocked_by: §1. A toned wall behind the chapter-opener title box was exactly the borrowed legibility §1 measured; the title now carries its own `card`, so the risk is gone. proof/title-ground.html measures the card on a dusk wall as the closure.
_timeOfDayShipped.day_not_shipped: DELIBERATELY. The set is lit by one warm desk lamp and one cold monitor and every cast shadow derives from those two. At dusk that is still true — the light outside is failing and the lamp is still the source. In daylight it is false: the lamp would not be the brightest thing in the room and every shadow would point the wrong way. Shipping `day` means a relight, which is a much bigger job than a wall tone. engine/plates.js room() still accepts "day"; no asset uses it.

figures/short-interest-16x9.note: §3.1. REPLACES figures/big-number-l2 in short-interest's evidence beat. Four quantities that mean nothing individually — the one proportion among them (shares short against float) is drawn as a proportion, so the reader does not divide anything.
figures/short-interest-16x9.renderer_contract: do NOT fill the `float` region: its outline is already drawn and it is the reference. Fill `short` from the left to (sharesShort / float) of the width. `days` and `borrow` are figures, not bars — they are a duration and a rate, and drawing them as bars invites a comparison that means nothing.
figures/short-interest-16x9.refuses: nothing is pre-coloured and nothing is marked. A 30%-of-float short position is a squeeze setup or a nothing depending on who holds it and why; the script decides. No alarm colour, no threshold line.
figures/short-interest-16x9.purpose: short interest as a share of float with days-to-cover beside it — the two numbers that are only meaningful together.
figures/short-interest-16x9.caution: Do not use either number alone; the plate exists because one without the other misleads.

figures/short-interest-9x16.note: SHORTS use the `short` format's the-move or numbers beat. Same four slots; value budget 8 characters.
figures/short-interest-9x16.purpose: short interest as a share of float with days-to-cover beside it — the two numbers that are only meaningful together.
figures/short-interest-9x16.caution: Do not use either number alone; the plate exists because one without the other misleads.

charts/insider-flow-6-16x9.note: §3.2. Six Form 4 trades on a time axis, sized by value — a normal quarter's filings, where the individual trades are still the argument. figures/ownership is the static picture; this is the flow.
charts/insider-flow-6-16x9.renderer_contract: fill each mark-N region FROM axisY: upward for a purchase, downward for a sale. Direction is the data, exactly as a waterfall step can add or subtract. BOTH HALVES SHARE ONE SCALE — scaling them independently makes a $200k purchase look like a $4m sale, which is a verdict reached by arithmetic and the hardest kind to notice.
charts/insider-flow-6-16x9.refuses: no green, no red, no arrow. One ink, one weight, both ways, so a plate of all sells looks like a plate of all buys inverted.
charts/insider-flow-6-16x9.counts: 6 and 12, authored not elastic — an elastic plate re-derives its pitch at render time and the pitch has to stay still between cuts.
charts/insider-flow-6-16x9.purpose: six periods of insider buying and selling as discrete marks, not a line.
charts/insider-flow-6-16x9.caution: Marks not a line, deliberately: insider windows are events and a line between them claims a trend.

charts/insider-flow-6-9x16.note: six marks in portrait. The per-mark who row still fits here (16 characters).
charts/insider-flow-6-9x16.purpose: six periods of insider buying and selling as discrete marks, not a line.
charts/insider-flow-6-9x16.caution: Marks not a line, deliberately: insider windows are events and a line between them claims a trend.

charts/insider-flow-12-16x9.note: twelve marks — the case the plate exists for, where the PATTERN is the argument rather than any single trade. Not for a shot that shares the frame with the host.
charts/insider-flow-12-16x9.caution: per-mark who row is 12 characters here, which holds 'CFO' and not a name. The role is almost always the point anyway.
charts/insider-flow-12-16x9.purpose: twelve periods of the same, for a full two years of windows.

charts/insider-flow-12-9x16.caution: NO per-mark who row in this aspect: the box measures under six characters and an over-budget fill does not render, so the plate publishes one `who-note` line instead — e.g. 'all four officers'. Measured by budget.js, not chosen.
charts/insider-flow-12-9x16.purpose: twelve periods of the same, for a full two years of windows.

charts/macro-series-16x9.note: §3.3. A decades-long FRED series with recession bands. Same name as charts/line-6y, different plate: ten labelled decades, forty minor ticks, band regions, and a source line.
charts/macro-series-16x9.renderer_contract: FOUR band regions are published and none is filled. A recession's extent is data — when it began, when it ended — so fill only the bands the series actually spans and leave the rest empty; do not distribute four bands across the plot because four exist. Fill at LOW value behind the series: a band that out-contrasts the line has become the subject.
charts/macro-series-16x9.required: the `source` slot is not optional. A macro series with no provenance is the one chart on a real-numbers channel that nobody can check.
charts/macro-series-16x9.counts: no count variants — the periods are not the company's, so the six-period convention does not apply.
charts/macro-series-16x9.purpose: a background series the company does not control — rates, a commodity, an index — with the relevant band shaded.
charts/macro-series-16x9.caution: Context only. Never use it to imply the company caused the move.

charts/macro-series-9x16.note: ten decades in portrait is dense. Source budget 74 characters.
charts/macro-series-9x16.purpose: a background series the company does not control — rates, a commodity, an index — with the relevant band shaded.
charts/macro-series-9x16.caution: Context only. Never use it to imply the company caused the move.

structure/end-card-16x9.note: §3.4. The closing frame built AROUND YouTube's end-screen elements. structure/closing is a chapter plate and knows nothing about the platform; this one's layout is dictated from outside the kit, which is why it is a separate plate.
structure/end-card-16x9.keep_out: three zones published in meta.keepOut as fractions of the frame: two video cards and a circular subscribe. Measured: 0 slot overlaps and 0 authored marks reaching a zone on both aspects. The paper surface does extend under them, correctly — the platform draws opaque elements on top of a ground.
structure/end-card-16x9.renderer_contract: the `hand` slot is what the viewer does next in the host's own register — e.g. 'the ledger is in the description'. NOT 'like and subscribe': the platform is already drawing a subscribe button in the same frame, and saying it twice is worse than not saying it.
structure/end-card-16x9.caution: UNVERIFIED — the zone fractions are DESIGNED-AGAINST, not confirmed against YouTube's current published spec. They are in the manifest so that when someone checks them the plate is corrected in one place and the content band moves with them.
structure/end-card-16x9.duration: the platform draws its elements over the final twenty seconds. Held for less than that, the zones are empty for no reason.
structure/end-card-16x9.purpose: the closing card of a long.

structure/end-card-9x16.note: zones sit lower in portrait and the content band is above them rather than beside them.
structure/end-card-9x16.caution: UNVERIFIED zone fractions, as above — and shorts' end-screen behaviour differs from long-form, which I could not check at all.
structure/end-card-9x16.purpose: the closing card of a long.

structure/confession-ledger-16x9.note: §2, RECOMMENDED TREATMENT. A numbered, dated entry on a ruled sheet. The credibility is in the existence of the record rather than in this admission — 'no. 14, and I write them all down'. Any chapter may reach for it; resigned-close is its home.
structure/confession-ledger-16x9.renderer_contract: entry-no takes the ledger count the pipeline already holds, e.g. 'no. 14'. It is the treatment's whole argument, so a composite that leaves it empty should fall back to the statement treatment rather than render a ledger entry with no number.
structure/confession-ledger-16x9.refuses: no cross, no strike-through, no red, no rule through the old claim. All three bodies are ONE type role at ONE size — the plate cannot mark which is the bad one. If the script wants the old claim struck, that is annotations/strike-out, and worth arguing about first.
structure/confession-ledger-16x9.counts: three blocks, fixed: what I said / what happened / what I got wrong. Not a count variant — the shape IS the three steps.
structure/confession-ledger-16x9.purpose: the admission with its itemised specifics beneath.
structure/confession-ledger-16x9.caution: Longer read than confession-statement; do not use it for a one-line admission.

structure/confession-ledger-9x16.note: SHORTS use the 'short' format's the-turn beat. Body budget 37 characters a line at two lines, so the three statements have to be written short before the script is recorded, not trimmed after.
structure/confession-ledger-9x16.purpose: the admission with its itemised specifics beneath.
structure/confession-ledger-9x16.caution: Longer read than confession-statement; do not use it for a one-line admission.

structure/confession-statement-16x9.note: §2, the alternative. Three blocks as one continuous statement, one left edge, one type size, one rail with a spur into each block. The credibility is in the equal weight: nothing marks the third block as the bad one. Use it when the confession is the first one about this company and there is no count worth showing.
structure/confession-statement-16x9.purpose: the admission as a single statement at display size.
structure/confession-statement-16x9.caution: For an admission with a ledger of specifics behind it, use confession-ledger.

structure/confession-statement-9x16.purpose: the admission as a single statement at display size.
structure/confession-statement-9x16.caution: For an admission with a ledger of specifics behind it, use confession-ledger.

_titleGround.applies_to: every room/* key that declares a title slot — 22 plates, the whole chapter-opener set. NO NEW KEYS: §1 is a variant axis on existing plates, not a family, so gates.reachable_plates does not gain a row and nothing here needs a chapter type of its own.
_titleGround.switch: engine/build.js TITLE_GROUND — "card" (SHIPPED, since drop nine), or null | "scrim" | "slab". This note said null was shipped for three drops after the value changed; `decided` below said card the whole time, so the file disagreed with itself and the stale half read as evidence that the treatment was still off. One value for the whole library: a chapter opener whose ground changes between chapters is two channels.
_titleGround.renderer_contract: the chapter-opener shot template must read slots.title.colour and set the title in THAT palette role rather than assuming structure. Only the slab treatment moves it (to ground), but a template that assumes structure is the thing that breaks silently the day the slab is picked — the same class of failure as the borrowed legibility itself.
_titleGround.unchanged: slots.title keeps its box on every plate, so every existing chapter-opener composite lands where it always did. meta.titleGround publishes the panel box, whether it is opaque, and which slots it covers.
_titleGround.decided: CARD. engine/build.js TITLE_GROUND = "card" — an opaque taped card with its own rim and cast, on all 22 chapter openers. Chosen because it is the only treatment that makes contrast wall-independent (11.9:1 on every wall, spread 0.0) WITHOUT moving the type colour, so slots.title.colour stays `structure` and the chapter-opener shot template needs no change. The six room plates with no title slot take no ground. proof/title-ground.html holds the comparison it was chosen from.
_titleGround._staleNote: CORRECTED IN DROP TWELVE. This entry said the shipped value was null while `decided` said card. Both were in the same object. The lesson is the one the baselines already carry: a stale note someone trusts is worse than an absent one, and it applies to prose in a data file as much as to a number.

_quarters.section: §2 — the quarter. Ten assets: charts/bars-8q, charts/line-8q, figures/qoq-yoy, charts/seasonality-{4,6}y, both aspects each. Every chart in the kit was annual; the pipeline now reads a Quarters sheet carrying six to eight quarters, and this is where they land.
_quarters.pipeline: the Quarters sheet feeds all three. bars-8q/line-8q take the series as loaded; qoq-yoy needs THREE readings out of it (the quarter, the previous quarter, the same quarter a year ago) and computes two deltas from them; seasonality needs the sheet reshaped to four quarters by N years, which is a pivot rather than a slice.
_quarters.gate: all ten reach a chapter type below, so none is reported unreachable.

charts/bars-8q-16x9.note: eight quarters as columns. Cut it against charts/bars-6y in the same chapter — same margins, same tick convention, so the grid does not move when the period changes.
charts/bars-8q-16x9.counts: 8 quarters, fixed. Eight is two whole years, which is the shortest span a seasonal pattern is visible in; six would show Q4 once and invite exactly the comparison figures/qoq-yoy exists to stop.
charts/bars-8q-16x9.period_format: Q3'25 — five characters. NOT 'Q3 2025': the head boxes are budgeted at this column count and a seven-character label is an over-budget fill, which does not render at all.
charts/bars-8q-16x9.caution: never caption a Q3-to-Q4 rise on this plate as growth. Eight quarters is two years, so Q4 appears twice — the comparison belongs to figures/qoq-yoy. See meta.seasonalityWarning.
charts/bars-8q-16x9.purpose: eight quarters as columns, current quarter picked out.

charts/bars-8q-9x16.note: SHORTS. No per-column value row on this aspect — the box measures five characters at eight columns and an over-budget fill does not render, so the plate publishes one value-last callout. The other seven quarters are a shape, and the voice-over has them.
charts/bars-8q-9x16.purpose: eight quarters as columns, current quarter picked out.
charts/bars-8q-9x16.caution: 16:9. At phone scale eight columns is the crowding limit — see the shorts brief.

charts/line-8q-16x9.note: the same eight quarters as a path. Use it when the shape between quarters is the point rather than the size of each one; bars-8q when a single quarter is going to be named.
charts/line-8q-16x9.purpose: eight quarters as one series — two years at quarterly resolution.
charts/line-8q-16x9.caution: Use when the quarterly shape matters. If only the trend matters, line-6y is cleaner.

charts/line-8q-9x16.note: value-last only, same measurement as bars-8q-9x16.
charts/line-8q-9x16.purpose: eight quarters as one series — two years at quarterly resolution.
charts/line-8q-9x16.caution: Use when the quarterly shape matters. If only the trend matters, line-6y is cleaner.

figures/qoq-yoy-16x9.note: THE EDITORIAL INSTRUMENT, not a chart. Both readings of one quarter, equal weight, side by side. Put it immediately after a quarterly chart and immediately after any management claim about growth — it is the plate that answers 'is it moving?' with 'against what?'.
figures/qoq-yoy-16x9.renderer_contract: fill BOTH deltas or neither. A composite that fills qoq and leaves yoy empty is the single-figure resolution this plate was built to prevent, arriving by omission; the shot audit should error on it rather than render half the pair.
figures/qoq-yoy-16x9.refuses: there is no slot for a blended growth figure. A script that wants one growth number wants figures/big-number — and should be asked why.
figures/qoq-yoy-16x9.purpose: one measure at two horizons — against last quarter and against last year — with both deltas.
figures/qoq-yoy-16x9.caution: Do not use for two different measures; the plate asserts they are the same series.

figures/qoq-yoy-9x16.note: the cells STACK in this aspect rather than sitting side by side, and that is a re-author rather than a rotation: two half-width cells on a phone would cost the deltas two type steps, which costs the pair its weight against the figure above. Congruent stacked boxes keep both.
figures/qoq-yoy-9x16.renderer_contract: same as 16x9 — both deltas or neither.
figures/qoq-yoy-9x16.purpose: one measure at two horizons — against last quarter and against last year — with both deltas.
figures/qoq-yoy-9x16.caution: Do not use for two different measures; the plate asserts they are the same series.

charts/seasonality-4y-16x9.note: four quarters across, four years deep. The plate that makes seasonality self-evident, so the script stops asserting it and starts pointing at it. Cut it BEFORE any quarter-on-quarter claim in the chapter.
charts/seasonality-4y-16x9.counts: 4 or 6 years. The quarters are always four, so the count varies on years only.
charts/seasonality-4y-16x9.series: one hue, value ramped — oldest lightest, newest at full subject ink. Not four series colours. The ramp also means the year the script is about is the darkest thing on the plot.
charts/seasonality-4y-16x9.purpose: four years of quarters grouped, so the within-year pattern shows.
charts/seasonality-4y-16x9.caution: The portrait choice. Use this rather than seasonality-6y at 9:16.

charts/seasonality-4y-9x16.note: SHORTS: prefer this over -6y. Sixteen columns in a 9:16 plot is a 35-unit column; twenty-four is 23, which is the thinnest data mark in the kit.
charts/seasonality-4y-9x16.purpose: four years of quarters grouped, so the within-year pattern shows.
charts/seasonality-4y-9x16.caution: The portrait choice. Use this rather than seasonality-6y at 9:16.

charts/seasonality-6y-16x9.note: six years. Not for a shot that shares the frame with the host — twenty-four columns will not survive it. Same call as waterfall-5s.
charts/seasonality-6y-16x9.purpose: six years of quarters grouped — the fuller seasonal picture.
charts/seasonality-6y-16x9.caution: Twenty-four columns. 16:9 only; at 9:16 it reads as four groups rising rather than six dated years.

charts/seasonality-6y-9x16.note: shipped for completeness and for a long-form 9:16 cut.
charts/seasonality-6y-9x16.caution: meta.crowded — a 23-unit column, 46px delivered. Legible at desk distance and the thinnest mark in the library; prefer seasonality-4y-9x16 for a SHORT. UNVERIFIED at phone scale.
charts/seasonality-6y-9x16.purpose: six years of quarters grouped — the fuller seasonal picture.

_filingReader.section: §3 — what the filing reader found. Six assets: structure/language-shift and paper/headline-stack-{3,4}, both aspects each.
_filingReader.pipeline: the reader's output is a set of CHANGES — a risk factor that appeared, management language that shifted, a segment that moved. language-shift takes one of those as a pair of short phrases with their years; headline-stack takes the news the writer now receives, three or four items with a date and a source each.

structure/language-shift-16x9.note: the same thing, described two ways, a year apart. Put it where the filing reader's language diff is being read out — and after the original claim has been said aloud, not before.
structure/language-shift-16x9.renderer_contract: the phrase boxes hold TWO LINES at ~30 characters in 16:9 and ~21 in 9:16, measured. A pasted filing sentence is over budget and does not render, which is deliberate: a language shift is four or five words. If it needs a sentence it is a quote and wants cards/quote-pull.
structure/language-shift-16x9.emphasis: the plate draws NO diff. Strike the old phrase with annotations/strike-out and mark the new one with annotations/underline-tight, applied by the compositor when the script asks — the plate must not decide which half is the bad one.

_hostSeated.not_to_camera: CORRECTED. This instruction used to read 'and to any role a LONG chapter opener uses', which is how sitting-at-desk reached `to-camera` — a long chapter opener does use that role, so the instruction was followed exactly and produced a defect. to-camera is FRAMINGS-ONLY: it is the role the renderer swaps to for a room that declares hostAnchor: false, and a framing is a camera distance with no floor line to pin. sitting-at-desk declares floorLineY 1728, so in a floorless room one pick in three seats him on nothing. The wording above is fixed; if a merge already put it in to-camera, take it out. It stays in the pose roles, where a floor exists.
_hostSeated.the_invariant: A ROLE THE RENDERER SWAPS TO FOR A FLOORLESS ROOM MAY CONTAIN ONLY PLATES WITH floorLineY: false. Two plates qualify — host/close-up and host/medium — and the kit publishes the field on every host plate precisely so this is checkable rather than remembered. NOT proposing host/sitting-at-desk-close to satisfy it: the seated plate is a full figure at 0.739 of a standing height and meta.seated.heights exists so the compositor can scale it against that ratio, so making it a framing would break the scaling contract to fix a membership error.

Scaled like a standing pose he comes out 36% oversized, sitting in exactly the right place, and no still would show it.

_reachability.finding: DROP THIRTEEN. The reachability check reported six stems unreachable. Two of them — structure/said-happened-5 and structure/sensitivity — were already mapped here and always have been. The check compares BARE STEMS against a fragment that is keyed by ASPECT: 57 of 60 keys carry a -16x9 or -9x16 suffix, and only three (the host poses) are bare. So a stem lookup misses every aspect-qualified entry.
_reachability.consequence: It reports reachable plates as unreachable, which is the safer direction and still wrong — it puts two plates on a to-fix list that needed nothing, and it means the check cannot distinguish a real gap from a keying mismatch. The four genuine gaps in the same report (said-happened-3, said-happened-4, whiteboard-3, whiteboard-4) are now mapped above.
_reachability.proposed_fix: The check should resolve a stem as reachable if ANY aspect-qualified key under it resolves, or the fragment should be re-keyed to stems with a per-aspect override. NOT APPLIED — the check lives on the pipeline side, and which way it goes is a decision about whether a mapping is allowed to differ per aspect. It currently can and does: several portrait keys carry different beats from their landscape twin, so collapsing to stems would lose that.
_reachability.unverified: I have not seen the reachability check's source. This is inferred from its output against this file's keys, and it is the most likely explanation rather than a confirmed one.

_purposes.added: rebuild-12. Every plate asset now carries a purpose line and, where one applies, a caution. Before this, 0 of 95 had a purpose and the writer saw a bare name and a list of slot names.
_purposes.rule: audit rule 24 fails any plate asset with no purpose or no chapter type.
_purposes.form: purpose = what it is for, present tense, in the vocabulary a writer thinks in. caution = when NOT to use it, or which sibling to prefer.
_purposes.reached_by: A plate with no chapter_types must say how it IS reached. 22 entries are marks, shorts furniture, overlays and full-frame rooms — named by the writer as [SCRIBBLE:], by a fixed shot list, by the compositor or by room rotation, never by a chapter type. Rule 24 accepts either, and fails an entry with neither.

room/desk-front-b.purpose: the second TALK angle — monitor off his shoulder rather than behind his head. Every short uses a talk room, and the role had one member.
room/desk-front-b.caution: Dusk-safe. Prefer it over desk-front whenever the previous video opened on desk-front.

room/desk-front-low.purpose: the third TALK angle, camera at desk height so the surface is a foreground plane. For the beat where the paperwork matters as much as he does.
room/desk-front-low.caution: Dusk-safe. The desk eats the lower third — do not put a lower third or a caption there.

room/read-close.purpose: the second READ angle — tighter than desk-side, page raised into the light, monitor out of frame. read carries the opening and closing shot of ten of the sixteen chapters.
room/read-close.caution: Dusk-safe. No screen in frame, so do not use it for a beat that refers to what is on the monitor.

room/board-side.purpose: the second DIAGRAM angle, from the left, wall running away to the right with him at the near edge.
room/board-side.caution: NIGHT ONLY until the relight lands — the wall cast still falls from the daylight lamp across the open right half.

room/doorway-wide.purpose: the second EXIT angle, pulled back so the whole door and the corridor light are in frame. One angle closes every long.
room/doorway-wide.caution: NIGHT ONLY — the corridor spill is keyed to the night lamp and the wide frame shows the cast crossing the floor.

charts/solvency-ratio.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
charts/solvency-ratio.purpose: an insurer’s solvency ratio quarter by quarter on a fixed scale, against the 100% requirement and its own target range.
charts/solvency-ratio.caution: Solvency regimes differ (Solvency II, RBC, BSCR); say which, and never compare two insurers under different regimes on one plate.

charts/combined-ratio.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
charts/combined-ratio.purpose: claims and costs as a share of premiums, stacked per year on a fixed scale, against the 100% line where underwriting stops making money.
charts/combined-ratio.caution: Use the ratio excluding prior-year reserve releases if the company gives it, or say that releases flatter it; show reserve-development beside it.

figures/reserve-development.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
figures/reserve-development.purpose: for each accident year, the first reserve estimate and today’s estimate as two marks on one rail: whether an insurer is finding out its claims cost more than it said.
figures/reserve-development.caution: Recent years always move most; say how many years of development each has had. Adverse development in a young year is an early warning, not yet a verdict.

charts/macro-rates.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
charts/macro-rates.purpose: the policy rate above, the bank’s net interest margin below, each on its own scale, with the bank’s own disclosed sensitivity: how rates reach the income statement.
charts/macro-rates.caution: Deposit costs lag rates; the margin can fall while rates are still high. Use the company’s sensitivity, never one computed from these panels.

charts/macro-inflation.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
charts/macro-inflation.purpose: inflation in the company’s inputs above, its own price increases below: pricing power as whether the second line follows the first.
charts/macro-inflation.caution: Use the inflation series closest to the company’s costs (food, not headline CPI) and say which.

charts/macro-fx.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
charts/macro-fx.purpose: the dollar above, the currency effect on reported growth below: the gap between reported and constant-currency growth, explained.
charts/macro-fx.caution: Constant-currency growth is the company’s own measure; quote its definition. Hedging can delay the effect by quarters.

charts/macro-commodity.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
charts/macro-commodity.purpose: the commodity price above, the producer’s margin below: how much of the margin is the price and how much is the company.
charts/macro-commodity.caution: A margin that stops following the price is a cost story; say which costs. Quote the company’s own sensitivity.

charts/macro-wages.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
charts/macro-wages.purpose: wage growth above, store costs as a share of sales below: operating leverage going the wrong way.
charts/macro-wages.caution: Costs as a share of sales rise when sales fall even if wages do not; show same-store sales alongside before blaming wages.

peers/sector-ranking.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
peers/sector-ranking.purpose: all eleven sectors’ returns over one period, ranked, as bars from zero on a fixed symmetric scale, with the market as one line down every row: where the episode’s sector ranked.
peers/sector-ranking.caution: Name the index family (the sectors must come from one index) and the period in the unit line. Total return, with dividends, unless the voice-over says otherwise.

charts/sector-vs-market.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
charts/sector-vs-market.purpose: one sector against the market over one period, both rebased to 100 on one scale, the gap NOT filled: the two are compared, not added, and the callout carries the gap.
charts/sector-vs-market.caution: Both lines from the same index family and both total return. Rebase at the start of the period the voice-over names, never at a low.

structure/said-happened-guidance.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
structure/said-happened-guidance.purpose: four things management guided against what was reported, with a tie marked only where the two contradict: a guidance record.
structure/said-happened-guidance.caution: Quote the guidance as given, with its date. Mark a contradiction only where the outcome is the opposite, not merely short.

structure/said-happened-capital.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
structure/said-happened-capital.purpose: four capital-allocation promises against what was done, contradictions tied.
structure/said-happened-capital.caution: A changed plan is not a broken promise if it was announced with reasons; say so where it was.

structure/said-happened-strategy.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
structure/said-happened-strategy.purpose: a strategy as it was announced each year against what happened to it.
structure/said-happened-strategy.caution: Use each year’s plan as announced that year, not as restated later.

structure/revision-trail-up.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
structure/revision-trail-up.purpose: how the consensus estimate moved across five dates, with the move called at each step, in the direction the market was being surprised.
structure/revision-trail-up.caution: Estimates rise into good news and fall after bad; say what each move followed, or the trail reads as momentum.

structure/revision-trail-target.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
structure/revision-trail-target.purpose: the average analyst price target across six dates, with each cut called.
structure/revision-trail-target.caution: Targets trail the price; a falling target is often the price being described, not predicted. Say so.

structure/revision-trail-revenue.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
structure/revision-trail-revenue.purpose: how the revenue forecast for one year moved across four dates.
structure/revision-trail-revenue.caution: The same fiscal year throughout; when the year rolls, start a new trail.

charts/surprise-vs-reaction.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
charts/surprise-vs-reaction.purpose: each quarter’s earnings surprise against the next day’s share move, on two fixed scales: whether beating still moves the stock.
charts/surprise-vs-reaction.caution: A day’s move has other causes (guidance, the market). Say what else was announced when a beat is followed by a fall.

peers/peer-rank.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
peers/peer-rank.purpose: one measure for the company and its peers, ranked, the company in attention and the peer median as a line: where it stands among the companies it is compared with.
peers/peer-rank.caution: Name how the peers were chosen. The line is the peer MEDIAN here, not the market; the legend must say so.

paper/risk-factor-diff.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
paper/risk-factor-diff.purpose: the changes to a company’s risk factors between two filings, as lines marked added, removed or reworded: what the lawyers decided the company must now warn about.
paper/risk-factor-diff.caution: Quote the filing’s words, not a paraphrase, in the reworded lines. Boilerplate changes are not news; leave them out.

paper/footnote-spotlight.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
paper/footnote-spotlight.purpose: one footnote quoted, with the sentence that matters underlined and its figure pulled out: the thing an annual report says quietly.
paper/footnote-spotlight.caution: Quote exactly and give the note and page. Pull out a figure only if the note states it.

charts/capital-returned.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
charts/capital-returned.purpose: dividends and buybacks as a share of free cash flow, stacked per year, against the 100% line: above it, the returns are funded from the balance sheet.
charts/capital-returned.caution: Say how the excess over 100% was funded (debt, cash on hand, disposals). A year over the line is not wrong; a run of them is the story.

structure/event-calendar.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
structure/event-calendar.purpose: the next dates that could move the shares on one rail over a fixed window, numbered, with the list saying what to watch at each: the episode’s closing checklist.
structure/event-calendar.caution: Only confirmed dates. An expected date the company has not announced goes in the voice-over, not on the rail.

structure/chapter-bumper.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
structure/chapter-bumper.purpose: the frame between chapters: the chapter number large, its title and the episode. Two seconds over room tone.
structure/chapter-bumper.caution: The title is the chapter’s claim in five words or so, not its topic. “Where the cash goes”, not “Cash flow”.

overlays/source-tag.reached_by: writer names it in a [PLATE:] tag; gated by chapter type
overlays/source-tag.purpose: where the figure on screen came from, as an alpha strip over a plate or the room: document, note and page.
overlays/source-tag.caution: Name the document and the page, never just “company filings”. One source per tag; two figures from two sources are two tags.

shorts/short-number.reached_by: the shorts writer names it; one per short
shorts/short-number.purpose: a short’s one number, set large in the safe area, with one line of context and its source.
shorts/short-number.caution: One number. If the short needs two, it is two shorts or a long plate.

shorts/short-quote.reached_by: the shorts writer names it; one per short
shorts/short-quote.purpose: a short’s one quote, large, with who said it and when, and the fact that makes it matter in the date line.
shorts/short-quote.caution: Quote exactly from a transcript and date it. The date line carries the irony; the quote is never edited to sharpen it.

shorts/short-chart.reached_by: the shorts writer names it; one per short
shorts/short-chart.purpose: a three-second chart: one line, its last point, and the change as the big figure.
shorts/short-chart.caution: One line and no grid. If it takes more than three seconds to read, use a long plate.

overlays/wipe-sweep.reached_by: the assembler, between two shots; never the writer
overlays/wipe-sweep.purpose: a hatched cover sweeps left to right; for moving on within a chapter. Eight frames, played once, alpha outside the cover.
overlays/wipe-sweep.caution: Cut the two shots under frame 4, where the cover is full. At most one wipe a minute; the plain cut is the default.

overlays/wipe-page.reached_by: the assembler, between two shots; never the writer
overlays/wipe-page.purpose: a sheet rises from the bottom edge and leaves at the top; for going to a document or a plate. Eight frames, played once, alpha outside the cover.
overlays/wipe-page.caution: Cut the two shots under frame 4, where the cover is full. At most one wipe a minute; the plain cut is the default.

overlays/wipe-blinds.reached_by: the assembler, between two shots; never the writer
overlays/wipe-blinds.purpose: slats close and reopen; for the cut into a new chapter, under the bumper. Eight frames, played once, alpha outside the cover.
overlays/wipe-blinds.caution: Cut the two shots under frame 4, where the cover is full. At most one wipe a minute; the plain cut is the default.
